chapter_title: Also concerning the Catechumen; shall he be saved

fills.notes: The sequence contrasts temporary companionship with inevitable separation. The substrate register favors an impersonal gnomic turn (“he knows that … they will separate”).
Travel-companions separate “each one (goes) to his own road/day.” The immediate context is lodging “by days and months,” so “day” is the natural term for each one’s allotted segment/time.
The logic is: when separation comes, none can take the house’s valuables with him. A negation is required to block possession/appropriation.
Matches the earlier “house for rent” and keeps the correspondence: worldly supports are hired/temporary, not owned. “rental house” also prepares the borrowed-vessels image.

Retain the editor’s restoration: the clause needs a smooth, non-effortful ascent after purification and formation of the “light image,” expressing ascent by affinity/weightlessness rather than struggle.

assessment: Most gaps are tightly constrained by the ‘lodging/rent/borrowed vessels’ correspondence: worldly relations and goods are temporary instruments, returned to their owner. Exact phrasing of the travel-separation clause is less recoverable, but the required logical joints (knowledge of separation, negation of taking, identification of the house as rented) are clear.
